[[File: Colours of Offaly.svg|border|20px]] [[Brian Whelahan]]{{Cite web |last=Stapleton |first=Shane |date=2018-12-17 |title=Managing the gap with Brian Whelahan |url=https://aib.ie/gaa/blog/2018/12/manging-the-gap-with-brian-whelahan |access-date=2025-03-05 |website=AIB |language=en-GB}} | team = Offaly | titles = 4th | captain = [[Hubert Rigney]]{{Cite journal |date=2020-05-31 |title=Hubert Rigney's 1998 All-Ireland winning speech |url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2020/0531/1143694-hubert-rigney-1998-all-ireland-winning-speech/ |journal=RTE |language=en}} | manager = [[Michael Bond (hurling manager)|Michael Bond]] | team2 = Kilkenny | captain2 = [[Tom Hickey (hurler)|Tom Hickey]] | manager2 = [[Kevin Fennelly]]{{Cite web |last=Keys |first=Colm |date=2015-09-03 |title=Fennelly admits he could never match Cody's level of commitment |url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/fennelly-admits-he-could-never-match-codys-level-of-commitment/31498726.html |access-date=2025-03-05 |website=Irish Independent |language=en}} | totalgoals = | totalpoints = | topscorer = [[File: Colours of Offaly.svg|border|20px]] [[John Troy (hurler)|John Troy]] (2–31) | previous = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1997|1997]] | next = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1999|1999]] }} The '''All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship of 1998''' (known for sponsorship reasons as the '''Guinness Hurling Championship 1998''') was the 112th staging of [[Ireland]]'s premier [[hurling]] competition. [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] won the championship, beating [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] 2–16 to 1–13 in the [[1998 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]] at [[Croke Park]], [[Dublin]].{{Cite web |last=Galvin |first=Kieran |date=2023-07-26 |title=Silver jubilee of 1998 Offaly victory marked in Croke Park |url=https://www.offalyindependent.ie/2023/07/26/silver-jubilee-of-1998-offaly-victory-marked-in-croke-park/ |access-date=2025-03-05 |website=Offaly Independent |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=McIntyre |first=Niall |date=2024-07-26 |title=Galway's All-Ireland Winning Heroes Of 1998: Where Are They Now? |url=https://www.balls.ie/gaa/galway-1998-where-are-they-now-605670 |access-date=2025-03-05 |website=Balls.ie |language=en}} == Team changes == === To Championship === Promoted from the [[All-Ireland Intermediate Hurling Championship]] * London === From Championship === Regraded to the [[All-Ireland Intermediate Hurling Championship]] * Westmeath ==Format== 1998 was the second year that the controversial "back door" or qualifier system was used in the All-Ireland Championship. While the two provincial final winners automatically qualify for the All-Ireland semi-finals the two defeated provincial teams join [[Galway GAA|Galway]] and the [[Ulster]] provincial final winners in two "quarter-finals". The two winners from these two games qualify for the semi-finals where they meet the Leinster and Munster winners. In 1998 [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] and [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] were the two teams to benefit from the qualifier system.{{Cite web |last=Hurley |first=Denis |date=2021-08-20 |title=Cork v Limerick All-Ireland will be eighth repeat meeting in back-door era |url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-40361768.html |access-date=2025-03-05 |website=echo live |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Nolan |first=Pat |date=2020-11-02 |title=The back door: Teams who went from qualifiers to All-Ireland hurling champions |url=https://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/hurling-news/back-door-teams-who-went-22946045 |access-date=2025-03-05 |website=Irish Mirror |language=en}} ==Semi-final controversy== The All-Ireland semi-final replay between [[Clare GAA|Clare]] and [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] ended in controversy when the referee, [[Jimmy Cooney (Galway hurler)|Jimmy Cooney]], mistakenly ended the game five minutes earlier than he had intended. At the time of the early stoppage, the score was 1–16 to 2–10 in favour of Clare. When the whistle blew there was disarray in [[Croke Park]] as the disgruntled Offaly supporters began a sit-down protest on the pitch.{{Cite web |last=Mac Donncha |first=Garry |date=2007-03-17 |title=Scannal – Long Hot Summer |url=https://www.rte.ie/tv/scannal/scannalhurling.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090212020103/https://www.rte.ie/tv/scannal/scannalhurling.html |archive-date=2009-02-12 |access-date=2025-03-05 |website=RTE One}} A Kildare v. Kerry IHC game planned for afterwards had to be cancelled.{{Cite web |last=Harrington |first=Eoin |date=2023-01-24 |title=Six GAA Sagas That Ended In Replays Being Ordered |url=https://www.balls.ie/gaa/gaa-replays-sagas-540513 |access-date=2025-03-05 |website=Balls.ie |language=en}} Clare graciously agreed to have the game replayed. In the re-fixture in Thurles 6 days later, the result was reversed with Offaly winning the game on a score of 0–16 to 0–13.{{Cite journal |last=Diallo |first=Raf |date=2024-07-03 |title=When Offaly got off the canvas to hit back at the Cats |url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2024/0703/1458031-when-offaly-got-off-the-canvas-to-hit-back-at-the-cats/ |journal=RTE |language=en}} ==All-Ireland final== As a result of the new qualifier system of games for the second year in a row, the All-Ireland final was contested by two teams from the same province. However, this year the final was a repeat of the [[Leinster]] final with [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] taking on [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]. Offaly were playing in their Third All-Ireland Final of the 1990s (having won against Limerick in 1994 and lost to Clare in 1995).
